dispersion_assumption.justification: The Level A synthetic harness lacks realistic credit outcome variables. Therefore, CV=0.60 is registered strictly as a conservative design parameter to ensure adequate statistical power against high-variance human behavioral data. It is NOT an empirical estimate of the target population's variance.

rationale: CV=0.60 is frozen as a deliberately conservative planning bound selected before scientific data generation. It is not an estimate derived from the Level-A synthetic harness and must not be interpreted as an empirical population parameter.
literature_basis: Van Belle & Martin (1993), The American Statistician, Sample Size as a Function of Coefficient of Variation and Ratio of Means.
Wolfe & Carlin (1999), Controlled Clinical Trials, Sample-size calculation for a log-transformed outcome measure.
